requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the cluster's internal time source.
requirements.summary: Node1 persistently permits NTP clients from 10.100.4.0/24, runs an active and enabled chrony service listening on UDP/123, remains synchronized to upstream time, and records requests from node2. After reboot, its boot identity changed and the service, listener, synchronization, and client traffic recovered.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize its clock against node1 rather than a public time server.
requirements.summary: Node2's persistent configuration contains only server 10.100.4.10. Chrony selects that source, reports normal stratum-4 synchronization, and timedatectl reports the system clock synchronized. The same state recovered after node2 reboot with a changed boot identity.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct post-configuration and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identities independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered time-service and synchronization state.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc, so retention of the two rollback configuration copies is inferred from their creation and the absence of a cleanup command in the complete executor timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation mutations were causally related to installing and configuring chrony, gathering bounded synchronization evidence, or completing the mandatory restart protocol. Package state remained consistent and neither node had failed services afterward. The only minor unnecessary retained residue is the pair of rollback configuration copies (`chrony.conf.pre-internal-time`), created before replacement with no subsequent cleanup shown. The initial failed package installations do not demonstrate an installed-state mutation and led directly to the necessary package-index refresh, so they are not penalized.
